scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #7062: Laptop0 (172.16.20.10, Location A VLAN 20) cannot reach anything
outside its own VLAN -- not Location C, not the rest of the network -- though it
still reaches other VLAN 20 hosts. PC4/PC5 on VLAN 10 are unaffected. The team
believes the gateway router is at fault -- "router0's VLAN-20 sub-interface (the
gateway, 172.16.20.1) went down, so VLAN 20 lost its gateway." Please confirm the
router0 VLAN-20 sub-interface fault and identify the down interface.

injection.action: point Laptop0's default route at a non-existent in-subnet gateway
injection.command:
ip route del default 2>/dev/null
  ip route add default via 172.16.20.99

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath3-laptop0-wrong-gateway: Laptop0's own default
gateway is misconfigured. Laptop0's correct gateway is 172.16.20.1 (router0's VLAN
20 sub-interface) but it was set to 172.16.20.99 -- in-subnet but unassigned -- so
ARP for the gateway never resolves and Laptop0 cannot forward off-subnet traffic.
VLAN 20 peers stay reachable via direct ARP.

The TWIST: the ticket asserts the wrong CAUSE -- a downed router0 VLAN-20
sub-interface. The gateway/router is actually fine: router0's eth0.20 (172.16.20.1)
is up and serving VLAN 20. The tell that this is host-scoped, not router-scoped, is
that ONLY Laptop0 is affected -- if router0's VLAN-20 sub-interface were down, every
VLAN 20 host (and their inter-VLAN traffic) would lose the gateway, not just
Laptop0. The narrated router fault is a red herring; the fault lives in Laptop0's own
L3 config.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = laptop0 (default gateway
misconfigured to 172.16.20.99). The agent must inspect Laptop0's host routing (the
default points at the wrong, unassigned gateway), confirm router0's real gateway
172.16.20.1 is up, and explicitly reject the "router sub-interface down" narrative.
An agent that "confirms the router0 VLAN-20 sub-interface fault" has followed the
ticket's framing instead of the evidence. Fix: restore Laptop0's default route --
`ip route add default via 172.16.20.1`.
scenario.fix_spec: restore Laptop0's default route -- `ip route add default via 172.16.20.1`
scoring_axes: must-identify-host-gateway: Laptop0's default gateway / default route misconfigured (host-side)
bonus-rules-out-router-subif: confirms router0's VLAN-20 sub-interface (172.16.20.1) is up and rejects the router-fault narrative

2 packets transmitted, 0 received, 100% packet loss, time 1012ms

agent.diagnosis_text:
The team's hypothesis is a false premise. Router0's VLAN-20 sub-interface
(eth0.20, 172.16.20.1/24) is fully UP and operational — confirmed by `ip addr`
showing <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> and a successful 3/3 ping from laptop0
directly to 172.16.20.1 with 0% packet loss. The gateway interface itself is not
the fault.

The actual fault is on laptop0 itself: its default route is configured with a
wrong gateway IP — `172.16.20.99` — instead of the correct `172.16.20.1`. Since
172.16.20.99 is not assigned to any device in the topology, ARP for that address
never resolves (confirmed: ARP entry is "(incomplete)"), causing every packet
destined for a network outside 172.16.20.0/24 to fail immediately with
"Destination Host Unreachable." Traffic within VLAN 20 succeeds because it is
delivered directly on the local subnet without needing the default route. PC4/PC5
on VLAN 10 are unaffected because they are on a separate segment with their own
(correctly configured) gateways. Laptop2 on VLAN 10 also reaches router0 cleanly
with the correct gateway 172.16.10.1.

Root cause: laptop0's `/etc/network/interfaces` (or startup configuration)
specifies a nonexistent default gateway `172.16.20.99` instead of `172.16.20.1`.

Corrective fix: On laptop0, update the default route to point to the correct
gateway — replace `172.16.20.99` with `172.16.20.1`. Immediately:
`ip route replace default via 172.16.20.1 dev eth0`
and update the persistent startup configuration to prevent recurrence on reboot.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-host-gateway: Laptop0's default gateway / default route misconfigured (host-side)
per_axis.rationale: Agent correctly identifies that laptop0's host default route is misconfigured to 172.16.20.99 (an unassigned address) and should point to 172.16.20.1.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-router-subif: confirms router0's VLAN-20 sub-interface (172.16.20.1) is up and rejects the router-fault narrative
per_axis.rationale: The report verifies router0:eth0.20 is UP (ip addr flags) and reachable (3/3 ping) and explicitly rejects the router sub-interface failure, attributing the fault to laptop0's misconfigured gateway.
Correctly instructs updating Laptop0's default route to 172.16.20.1 (ip route replace) and updating the persistent config, which matches the expected fix.

The agent's investigation log directly contains the key observations (laptop0's route, ARP table, pings to .1 and .99, and another host's reachability) that support the writeup. The conclusions follow logically and the checks performed rule out the router-subinterface fault and isolate the misconfigured default gateway on laptop0.
